sources_considered.why: Dated primary benchmark launch report provides AI scores and evaluation conditions.
Dated primary report directly describes failures on compositional reasoning tasks.
Original May paper provides average human performance and benchmark methodology.
Reproduces the benchmark organization's dated July 10 announcement of improved performance; used only as adjacent-period context.

receipt.public_excerpt: public AI reasoning systems achieve only single-digit percentage scores.

evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark's launch evaluation records low AI task-solving rates. These are historical launch results, not a claim that the same exact ceiling persisted through July.

evidence_items.locator: Each task requires deeper, human-like thinking; 2. Compositional Reasoning
evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark authors directly report difficulty combining interacting rules. This supports the compositional part of the claim without inferring a subset result from overall accuracy.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5, human testing results immediately before section 6

receipt.public_excerpt: The average test-taker solved 66% of tasks they attempted.

evidence_items.explanation: The reported average human success rate supplies a reference for judging the low AI scores. It is distinct from the separate finding that every retained task was solved by at least two people.

evidence_items.publisher: ARC Prize Foundation, reproduced by Thread Reader App
evidence_items.locator: ARC Prize thread dated July 10, 2025, opening sentence

receipt.public_excerpt: Grok 4 (Thinking) achieves new SOTA on ARC-AGI-2 with 15.9%

evidence_items.explanation: The adjacent-day announcement establishes substantial progress beyond the launch scores, while remaining well below the reported average human result. It is outside the target period and is not used as decisive evidence about what was public before Marcus posted.
